newsitem.title: UK: Dlr drifts down in Europe as year draws to a close.
newsitem.headline: Dlr drifts down in Europe as year draws to a close.

text.p: The dollar drifted down in late European business as the 1996 trading year drew to a close. The European forex market is now effectively closed and will reopen for business on Thursday January 2.

The dollar was hit after November U.S. single-family home sales rose 14.2 percent and as December consumer confidence increased to 113.8. The strong data hit both U.S. treasuries and Wall Street, taking the dollar down.
At 1525 GMT the dollar was at 1.5385/95 marks and 115.71/81 yen, down from an early 1.5546/53 and 116.18/28 and Monday's 1.5563/69 and 115.82/92.

Earlier the dollar had renewed its upward move on the yen to a fresh 45-month peak of 116.40. Weak Japanese asset markets, reflecting concerns about the economic outlook and weak economic recovery, have helped to boost the dollar against the yen, said analysts.
